  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The post-open sweep closes every listed discovery PR whose head branch differs from replacement_branch without comparing the consumer HEAD SHAs in the branch names, so a stale concurrent run can close a newer PR as superseded_by_newer_pr.
  WHY: validation-refresh.yml:53-65 keys the concurrency group on branch_name, so runs with different branch_name inputs can overlap on one consumer. Severity disagreement: MAJOR (minimax, openai) vs NIT (z-ai); the highest is used.
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:1141-1197 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The human-commit recheck and the PR close are separate operations, so a person can push a non-codex-bot commit after `gh pr view --json commits` returns and before `gh pr close` runs.
  WHY: The runner would then close a PR containing a human commit, contrary to the documented guarantee at README.md:4375. Severity: MAJOR.
- scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:858-866 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A PR kept as kept_human_commits in the first sweep stays in the returned list with its listing-time bot_only=True, so the second sweep re-checks it and logs another kept_human_commits line.
  WHY: The cost is one redundant `gh pr view` call and one duplicate log line per such PR per cycle. Nothing is closed wrongly. Sonnet rated it NIT; minimax and z-ai raised it only as a hardening suggestion.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:1087-1092 (also scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py lines 659-664 and 858-866, .github/workflows/validation-refresh.yml line 64) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The sweep closes any listed PR whose head_branch differs from replacement_branch without comparing the SHA portions of the branch names. Two runs with different branch_name inputs sit in different concurrency groups, so the slower run (older consumer_head_sha) can close the newer PR as superseded_by_newer_pr.
  WHY: Reproducer: run A (branch_name=smoke-X) opens PR #100 on SHA S1. Run B (branch_name=smoke-Y, S2 a descendant of S1) opens PR #200 and finishes its sweep first. Run A then lists open PRs, sees #200, and closes it with a comment pointing at #100. #200 carries the newer SHA and needs a manual reopen. The suggested fix is to close only when the listed PR's SHA is an ancestor of or equal to the current run's SHA.
- HARDENING (risk score 1): scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py, the `list_open_discovery_prs` --json flag (around line 985). The `commits` field is fetched for up to 100 PRs per consumer per cycle even though the per-PR re-check guards correctness. It is advisory only (0 lines changed), to be applied only if the listing call is observed to be slow.
- HARDENING (risk score 2): scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py, close_superseded_discovery_prs lines 1136-1176 (the re-check block). A kept_human_commits PR keeps bot_only=True in the returned list, so the second pass at scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:858-866 wastes another `gh pr view`, `gh pr close` and log line. Suggested fix: dataclasses.replace(pr, bot_only=False) (about 4 lines).
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

  PROBLEM: The replacement sweep treats every discovery PR on a different branch as older, without comparing the PRs' consumer HEAD SHAs.
  WHY: validation-refresh.yml:53-65 permits concurrent runs with different branch_name inputs. A run with a stale consumer clone can open its older-HEAD PR after a newer run has opened one, and this code then closes the newer PR as superseded_by_newer_pr. The stale PR stays open, so the consumer is left with the outdated proposal.

  WHY: A person can push a non-codex-bot commit after `gh pr view --json commits` returns and before `gh pr close` runs. The runner then closes a PR with a human commit, contrary to the documented guarantee at README.md:4375.

  SEVERITY: NIT

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/validation_discovery_bootstrap.py:~1085-1092 (close_superseded_discovery_prs, the `if replacement_branch is not None:` branch; second-pass call at scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py:855-865) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: In the post-open pass, every listed discovery PR whose head branch differs from replacement_branch is closed as superseded_by_newer_pr without comparing the head SHAs in the branch names (`<prefix>/<sha>/<type>`).
  WHY: The workflow concurrency group keys on branch_name (validation-refresh.yml:53-65), so a manual dispatch with a custom branch_name runs in parallel with the daily cron. A slower run on a stale clone can close the newer-head PR. The newer run's `success_*` dedup entry then suppresses re-proposal for 7 days.
- HARDENING (risk score 1): scripts/validation_refresh_runner.py, the `_sweep_superseded_discovery_prs` return list (lines ~960-965) and the second-pass call at line 857. PRs kept as `kept_human_commits` (or `close_failed` from a re-check failure) keep bot_only=True and are re-checked in the post-open pass. Suggested fix: return dataclasses.replace(pr, bot_only=False) for them (about 4 lines).
